column1: # Real bond-fund anchors: the measurements the model's two bond relations are fitted FROM.
# Measured 2026-08-22: eight iShares funds, 19-24 years of history each, total returns from NAV
# plus reinvested distributions -- the same source and method as the TLT anchor, which that
# pipeline reproduces to 14.12% against the recorded 14.1%. The measurement window is part of the
# data: re-measuring over a different span, or with a different total-return convention, moves the
# fitted lines for reasons that are not errors.
# Checked by uni.apps.BondAnchorSuite and the `bond_anchor_tests` module in
# rust/examples/market_sim.rs. Both re-fit the lines below and assert they reproduce the constants
# their own twin carries; neither needs the other language installed.
#   duration    effective duration in years, as published by the fund -- MEASURED, never fitted
#   annVol      annualised standard deviation of daily total returns, %
#   d5 d10 d20  share of sessions more than 5/10/20% below the running peak
# The two fitted lines, and where each one is used:
#   d10    = 0.0397 * annVol - 0.0785  (floored at zero)   BondD10Slope / BondD10Intercept
#                                                          BOND_D10_SLOPE / BOND_D10_INTERCEPT
#   annVol = -0.07 + 0.937 * duration                      the duration scaling of SigmaNBond
# BOTH are fitted on the five TREASURIES only. The three credit rows are not inputs to either fit:
# they are the SCOPE of the +-0.35 band, which admits AGG (1.06) and LQD (0.71) and excludes HYG
# (0.50) because this model has no credit channel. That band is therefore a scope decision as much
# as a tolerance, and it is wider than the Treasuries' own scatter (0.79-1.04) for that reason.
